skill.name: playwright-browser-automation
skill.description: Automates browser testing with Playwright by detecting local development servers, generating temporary scripts, running interactions, and capturing screenshots.
skill.summary: Run Playwright browser automation for local web testing and UX validation.
skill.author: Claude Assistant

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Playwright browser automation helper, but it intentionally executes generated JavaScript locally and can install dependencies automatically. Most Markdown backtick, localhost URL, and schema UUID detections are false positives; the confirmed issues center on arbitrary code execution, external commands, weakened Chromium sandboxing, local port probing, and temporary file or screenshot handling.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before executing generated scripts or inline code, and document that scripts run with local user privileges.
Remove automatic npm install and npx playwright install from run.js, or gate them behind an explicit setup command the user approves.
Avoid --no-sandbox and --disable-setuid-sandbox unless the user explicitly runs in an environment that requires them.

remediation.issue: Temporary scripts and screenshots written to /tmp
remediation.suggestion: Use a private, permission-restricted temporary directory and delete generated scripts and screenshots after reporting results.
Remove prisma/schema.prisma from the published skill unless it is required for browser automation.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks are slow and easy to miss across forms, links, and screen sizes. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code run Playwright automation, capture screenshots, and validate web flows.
actual_capabilities: Detects common localhost development servers before running tests.
Runs generated Playwright scripts from files, inline arguments, or stdin.
Automates page visits, form filling, clicks, login checks, and link checks.
Captures screenshots for full pages and responsive viewport comparisons.
Provides helper functions for safe clicks, typing, cookie banners, tables, and retries.
limitations: Executes local JavaScript, so users must review generated scripts before running them.
May install Playwright and Chromium if dependencies are missing.
Primarily targets local development servers and user-provided URLs.
Screenshots and temporary scripts may contain sensitive page data.

use_cases.title: Check a local feature before commit
use_cases.description: Run a browser through a local development server and verify the main user path works.

use_cases.title: Validate responsive layouts
use_cases.description: Open a page at desktop, tablet, and mobile sizes and capture screenshots for review.

use_cases.title: Test common web flows
use_cases.description: Fill forms, submit login screens, follow links, and report visible failures.

prompt_templates.title: Test one local page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Playwright browser automation skill to find my local dev server and open the home page. Report the page title and any visible console errors.

prompt_templates.title: Capture responsive screenshots
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to test the current page on desktop, tablet, and mobile widths. Save screenshots and summarize layout issues you observe.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a form flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to open the contact form, fill realistic test values, submit it, and confirm whether a success message appears.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a full user journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to test the login journey, dashboard load, navigation links, and responsive behavior. Ask before using credentials or running generated scripts.

output_examples.input: Test the marketing page on my local dev server.
output: Opened the marketing page and captured desktop and mobile screenshots.
Reported the title, visible layout issues, and any broken navigation links.

output_examples.input: Check whether login redirects to the dashboard.
output: Detected multiple local servers and asked which one to test.
Ran the selected login flow with the provided test credentials.
Reported whether the dashboard URL and expected page elements appeared.

output_examples.input: Take a screenshot of the current page.
output_examples.output: The skill opened the target URL in Playwright, captured a full-page screenshot, and reported where it was saved.

best_practices: Review generated Playwright scripts before execution, especially when they use credentials.
Use local or test accounts and avoid production data during browser automation.
Clean up screenshots and temporary files after the result is no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated scripts against production sites without authorization.
Do not paste real passwords, tokens, or payment data into automated test prompts.
Do not treat screenshots as harmless if the page can display private data.

faq.question: Does this skill run real browser actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Playwright to launch a browser, navigate pages, interact with elements, and capture screenshots.

faq.question: Can it find my local development server?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks common localhost ports and asks which server to use if more than one is found.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with credentials?
faq.answer: Use test credentials when possible. Generated scripts and screenshots may expose sensitive data if handled carelessly.

faq.question: Where are generated scripts stored?
faq.answer: The skill documentation instructs writing scripts to /tmp and the executor creates temporary files in the skill directory.

faq.question: Can it test external websites?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide an authorized URL. You should not use it for sites where you lack permission to automate access.
